sources.shortCitation: Parlophone A6766, “Someone to Care for Me” [Victor Silvester and His Ballroom Orchestra]
sources.fullCitation: Victor Silvester and His Ballroom Orchestra. “Someone to Care for Me” / “My Day Begins and Ends with You.” Parlophone A6766, Australian pressing, 10-inch 78 rpm shellac disc. Discogs release 28032108, dated 1937 in the catalogue.
sources.title: Someone to Care for Me — Parlophone A6766
sources.creator: Victor Silvester and His Ballroom Orchestra
sources.researchNote: The photographed label confirms Parlophone A6766, manufacture in Australia, the orchestra and the “Someone to Care for Me” side’s Kaper–Jurmann credit. The year 1937 is supplied by Discogs, not printed on that label; it is treated as a reported issue date, not a recording-session date. Neither Gus Kahn’s lyricist credit nor Leo Feist’s sheet-music-publisher credit is established by this label. This is a separate orchestral recording, not Deanna Durbin’s film performance.

sources.fullCitation: Portrait of Professor Walther Gmeindl. Image from the Discogs artist page “Professor Walther Gmeindl” (artist ID 6548258).
sources.title: Professor Walther Gmeindl — portrait (Discogs)
sources.researchNote: Recorded as Discogs (discogs.com) presents it: the details given here follow that page rather than an examination of the object itself.

sources.shortCitation: Adler Electro 5713, “Ich weiß, daß du einst meinen Mund vergißt” / “Du lieber Geiger, spiel einen Tango für mich”
sources.fullCitation: Jazzorchester John Morris, with vocal refrain by Erik Garell. “Ich weiß, daß du einst meinen Mund vergißt” (2216), music by K. M. May and Dr. B. Kaper, words by Fr. Rotter and K. Brüll / “Du lieber Geiger, spiel einen Tango für mich” (2222), music by Dr. B. Kaper and German, words by Fritz Rotter. Both from Seitensprünge. Adler Electro, Bestell-Nr. 5713, 10-inch 78 rpm shellac disc, Germany, n.d. Discogs release 2950735; photographs of both labels.
sources.title: Ich weiß, daß du einst meinen Mund vergißt / Du lieber Geiger, spiel einen Tango für mich — Adler Electro 5713
sources.creator: Jazzorchester John Morris; Erik Garell, vocal refrain
sources.researchNote: Both photographed labels identify the performers and authors, Bestell-Nr. 5713 and the additional side numbers 2216 and 2222. The Discogs record supplies no issue date; the film’s 1931 date does not establish when this disc was released. The labels do not identify Edition Karl Brüll as publisher. References to Gloria and an unrelated YouTube transfer have been removed: this source documents the photographed Adler Electro issue.

sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester conducted by O. Dobrindt. “Ich bin der Hans im Glück” / “In 24 Stunden.” Odeon O-11810, shellac, 10-inch, 78 rpm, Germany, 1933. Discogs release 28872088.
sources.title: Ich bin der Hans im Glück / In 24 Stunden — Odeon O-11 810
sources.creator: Hans Albers; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, O. Dobrindt, conductor
sources.researchNote: Discogs identifies “In 24 Stunden” as matrix Be 10225-2 and the reverse as Be 10224. The recording date, take, Berlin studio and April 1933 release are independently supplied by the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de.
